summary: Keep readers, checkpoint copies and WAL observations on SQLite's opened database target rather than a caller path alias.

replay.detail: No projection or admission rule change and no added replay. Resolving the main filename is a bounded connection metadata read.

schema.detail: No table, index, trigger, storage marker or migration change. FULL synchronous durability and existing creation/open errors are preserved.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules, claim or replication algorithm change. Checkpoint source files and WAL sidecars use the same resolved target as the opened store.

compatibility.detail: Local Rust Store.path and ReadPool.path now retain SQLite's resolved file target for file stores; memory URIs retain their original shared-memory name. Callers wrapping mismatched writer/read-pool paths or modes are refused. No wire/API response or logical origin/key change. Database-size telemetry and runtime-start lock directories already derive from Store.path and therefore follow the physical target too.

downtime.detail: The source fix alone performs no installed relocation or restart. Ordinary deployment/restart and any later Operations relocation window require their own qualification; no restart duration or performance improvement is measured here.

manual.detail: This change authorizes no file copy, symlink/bind installation, live database action or configuration change. Operations must separately qualify the actual narrow relocation and path-derived runtime-start lock directory under the normal cut. Stop the old process before the new build opens the state, or run only one build per state directory: old alias-derived and new target-derived runtime-start locks do not exclude each other. Canonical naming is not protection against concurrent target or parent replacement.

recovery.detail: No database format changed. Returning to an earlier binary reintroduces caller-alias readers/sidecars/telemetry; do not treat it as safe for a symlink relocation without separate Operations review. Preserve the authoritative target and WAL and roll forward if the installed layout cannot support the prior path behavior; this source change supplies no live-store recovery operation.
